answer: Each identity claims one timber stand on a mesa bench, locks a 70-credit bond, and pays a stump-tally fee: the first stand costs 29 credits, the kth costs 29+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7022 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,525,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A meadow baseline survey line fixes the stand boundary, and an auditor recounts stumps and matches timber tags to the stand register; a short tally or mismatched tag burns the bond. A rented-stand ring fails because rented tags carry no signature from the renter's key, so both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 29 once and reclaims the bond.
